# Library pathways: the map, the real cases and the limitations (2026-11-12)

**Generated file.** Built by `docs/program/evidence/library-pathways/build-page.js.txt` from `docs/program/library-pathways/` (map.json, params.json, engine.js, limitations.json, cases.json) and the page copy in `docs/program/evidence/library-pathways/page-src/text.json`. The owner reads `docs/program/library-pathways/index.html`, built from the same data in the same run. Do not edit this file by hand.

**Rules.** This record maps and measures. It contains no fixes and no judgment on whether the library reaches its goal. Tags: [M] Measured on this PC, in the owner's repositories or session records. [S] Taken from an outside study or the vendor's price list. [G] A guess. A number the model computes takes the weakest tag of its inputs. Every computed number here uses at least one guess, so it is tagged G. In a table, the tag in the heading applies to the column.

## 1. The map

One episode: a fix-sized piece of work of about ten cheap calls, where a result is produced and checked. Cheap-call equivalents. One call by the cheap model (Sonnet) costs 1. Lookup, screen, carry and handoff are paid at the cheap tier. One period is 30 days. The number of periods is a run setting: it is chosen, never drawn and never swung.

The graph has 40 [M] states and 83 [M] branches over eleven stages and an outcome. It has 57 [M] settings: 55 [M] unknowns drawn in the runs (46 [M] guesses, 6 [M] from outside studies, 3 [M] measured), plus the horizon and the Opus price ratio, which are fixed.

| Way of working | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Strong model directly | Opus does the work. If the gate catches a wrong answer, Fable tries. No library. |
| Cheap model with the ladder | The cheap model tries first. A caught failure gets one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable. No library. |
| Cheap model with the library | The same ladder, plus the library: a lookup before the cheap attempt, and Opus or Fable solves written back as entries. |

| Design step (walkthroughs) | Model stage(s) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. A task arrives: what is in the window | Trigger |
| 2. Trigger: does anything start a lookup, and when | Trigger |
| 3. Query: what is asked, in what words | Result of the lookup |
| 4. Match: what comes back | Result of the lookup |
| 5. Delivery: which window receives it, and does it stay | Delivery |
| 6. Use: the cheap model adapts and applies it | Screen: does it apply?; Cheap attempt |
| 7. Check: what decides the result equals the strong model's | Gate |
| 8. Failure and the ladder: how failure is noticed, what goes up to Opus, then Fable | Cheap retry; Opus; Fable |
| 9. Capture: what is written, by whom, when, from what | Capture |
| 10. Afterlife: what happens to the entry later | Afterlife of an escape |

The walkthroughs used the design's ten steps. The model splits the work into eleven stages and an outcome. This match between them was set by hand: step 1 (what is in the window) has no stage of its own and is shown with the trigger; step 6 (use) covers the screen and the cheap attempt.

## 2. At the best values

All settings at the best value in params.json; horizon 12 periods. Every figure here is computed [G].

| Way of working | Cost per piece [G] | Wrong rate [G] | Cost at cheap / Opus / Fable [G] |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Strong model directly | 29.9 | 11.2% | 0.0 / 26.9 / 3.0 |
| Cheap model with the ladder | 25.7 | 21.2% | 12.5 / 12.3 / 0.9 |
| Cheap model with the library, first period | 26.4 | 21.2% | 12.8 / 12.5 / 1.0 |
| Cheap model with the library, last period | 26.6 | 21.4% | 12.9 / 12.7 / 1.0 |

| Library against | Cost ratio, first / last [G] | Wrong-rate ratio, first / last [G] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cheap model with the ladder (what the library itself adds) | 1.03 / 1.03 | 1.00 / 1.01 |
| Strong model directly (the owner's goal) | 0.88 / 0.89 | 1.90 / 1.91 |

Stocks at the start of the last period: 63.5 [G] good entries and 62.0 [G] bad. A ratio is the library's figure divided by the other way's figure. Below one: the library's figure is lower. Above one: it is higher.

**Loops in the stock drawing.** R1 (reinforcing) Bad entries bring more bad entries: More bad entries raise the share of bad entries a lookup returns. More wrong entries reach the cheap attempt and spoil work. More work climbs to Opus or Fable. More strong-tier solves and escapes get written, some of them bad. R2 (reinforcing) More entries, more look-alikes: Every entry, good or bad, raises the chance a misleading look-alike can be retrieved. Accepted look-alikes spoil work, more work climbs the ladder, and more entries get written. B1 (balancing) Good entries thin their own supply: More good entries fill the library. The cheap model is right more often with an entry in hand, so less work climbs to Opus or Fable, and fewer new entries are written. B2 (balancing) Good entries go stale: Each period a share of the good entries goes stale and moves to the bad stock. The more good entries there are, the more go stale.

## 5. Where the design worked in real cases

Same walks, same weight. Figures come from the walk records [M].

- f01-C3a (Same mistake, new session): A stored pdftoppm route served to the second wave would have saved 2 to 8 calls per agent across four Opus agents.
- f01-C4a (Same mistake, new session): One git flag with an exact error template, served before cloning, would have saved the 15 failed clones of 11-04.
- f10-3 (Existing notes over time): The pushed Python note worked at no extra cost: three agents carried its remedy in the same command as the probe, on 11-09 and 11-12.
- f08-1 (Across projects): The memory index put the long-paths fix into a sibling session before its first clone; that clone never failed.
- f05-4 (Races and flaky failures): A lookup by the failing test's name would have hit the root's entry, saving a wrong fixture commit, its revert, stopped runs and one Opus review.
- f05-3 (Races and flaky failures): The check held: an exact match to an old, fixed cause was tested, came back 'does not apply', and no wrong fix was applied.
- f06-C4 (Two correct pieces, one fault): After the first solve, a do-not-apply entry on the handoff's wrong advice stops a change that would let a 4-digit PIN be guessed without limit. CLAUDE.md already warns.
- f06-C2 (Two correct pieces, one fault): The action words 'enable dispatcher' reach the stored hazard, preventing the replay measured at 36 messages about months-old jobs, plus permanent suppressed rows.
- f03-C5 (Building new beside old): The builder's own words 'offline presence outbox' reach the right entry; had a lookup fired, it saves three days of stuck badges and a rework commit.
- f09-2 (The ladder in real life): A red check handed raw output to Fable, which fixed the defect in about a minute and wrote the rule, with its reason, within two minutes.
- f09-1 (The ladder in real life): The S02 entry, fetched at the S04 check, would have stopped the top tier's wrong premise: one finding's round trip saved.
- f07-4 (Research and design cases): A later change reused two stored traps and avoided at least two failed cloud builds; a later design reused one that cost about 15M helper tokens.
- f07-5 (Research and design cases): A design 'no' stored with its reason held for five months and was never argued again.
- f10-1a (Existing notes over time): The design's scan for fixes not on the main branch fits June exactly: it removes one of build 15's two causes and 16 days of broken main.
- f10-1b (Existing notes over time): The empty-value check promoted into the shared test run blocks that mistake for every agent and human, with no lookup.

## 6. Many runs

Most unknowns are guesses. So the model is run many times. Each run draws every unknown at random, evenly, from its range. The result is a spread, not one answer. 46 [M] of the 55 [M] drawn unknowns are guesses. **This spread follows from the assumed ranges. Change a range and it changes. It is not a measurement of the library.** This table: 1000 runs, seed 20261112, last period; the page runs its own with any seed and gives the same numbers for the same seed.

| Ratio (library over) [G] | 5 in 100 below | middle | 95 in 100 below | Moves it most (rank correlation, with tag) [G] |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Cost, against the ladder | 1.01 | 1.04 | 1.10 | c_write +0.42 [G], w_write +0.41 [G], p_visible +0.28 [G], n_cheap -0.27 [G], t_latent +0.21 [G] |
| Wrong rate, against the ladder | 1.00 | 1.01 | 1.08 | h_harm +0.38 [G], v_max +0.37 [G], f_false +0.33 [G], a_wrong +0.27 [S], need_latent -0.27 [G] |
| Cost, against strong directly | 0.47 | 0.90 | 1.81 | n_opus -0.74 [G], n_cheap +0.49 [G], o_opus +0.22 [G], rho_retry -0.17 [G], s_review +0.14 [G] |
| Wrong rate, against strong directly | 1.00 | 1.86 | 6.06 | o_opus +0.87 [G], o_fable +0.37 [G], s_review -0.17 [G], rho_retry -0.16 [G], g_tests_visible -0.09 [G] |

Share of runs where the library costs less and its wrong rate is no higher (last period): against cheap model with the ladder 0.0% [G]; against strong model directly 3.4% [G]. With 1000 runs, rank correlations closer than about 0.06 [G] are not well separated.

## 7. What the map leaves out

- **A model of the mechanism, not a forecast.** Its numbers follow from its settings. 46 [M] of the 55 [M] unknowns that are drawn are guesses.
- **Chosen cases, not a sample of work.** The 59 [M] cases were chosen because something went wrong. They show which routes exist and where steps break. They never show how often.
- **Case statuses are judgments.** Works, strains and breaks were set by the agents that walked the cases from the records. Another reader could set some differently.
- **One size of work.** Every piece of work is treated as about ten cheap calls. Real work varies far more in size, and a large piece is not the same as many small ones.
- **Calls are the same size inside a tier.** The cost unit is one cheap-model call. The price ratios are per token, so they equal the per-call ratio only if calls are the same size in every tier. On this PC's records an Opus call averaged about 222,000 [M] cache-read tokens and a Sonnet call about 440,000 [M]. On that data the per-call ratio would be near one, while the model fixes it at two.
- **Time and attention are not counted.** Tests at the gate cost nothing. Waiting, wall-clock time and the owner's attention are left out. A lookup counts as calls; a mechanical check, carrying an entry and a handoff cost cheap-call equivalents but count as no calls.
- **Pieces of work are independent.** A piece's kind, what the cheap model would do, what the library holds and whether a look-alike exists are combined by multiplying their chances. Real work clusters: a hard problem may also be the one the library lacks.
- **Averages, not one library.** The two stocks change by their expected amounts each period. A real library has one history, with luck in it. Each period is worked out on the stocks at its start, and staleness acts on those starting stocks.
- **Entries are all-or-nothing.** A good entry is good wherever it applies, and a bad one bad. Partly right shows up only as the composite 'some parts' result.
- **One pool of entries.** Projects are not separated. Facts that differ between projects act only through the look-alike and wrong-entry chances.
- **A wrong entry acts once.** A wrong accepted entry acts only at the cheap attempt. It does not follow the work up the ladder.
- **A fixed ladder and one gate.** One cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable, in that order. Real sessions skip rungs, repeat them, or end with the owner. The chance the gate catches a wrong output does not depend on which model made it.
- **Bad entries stay bad.** A bad entry turns good only when a found escape is repaired. Staleness moves good entries to bad, never the other way.
- **Two settings are fixed.** The number of periods is a chosen horizon, never drawn. The Opus price ratio has a range of one value, so the runs never vary it.
- **Ranges are drawn evenly and on their own.** If two unknowns move together in reality, the runs do not know it. The ranking measures steady rise or fall inside the ranges. It misses an effect that rises and then falls.
- **Some limitations act through nothing here.** 2 [M] limitations name no unknown, so the model cannot show them: LIM-44 (An error line is not always a failure); LIM-68 (Private details travel with entries).
- **Some tags are generous.** Several figures tagged M or S were measured on a different unit than the setting they stand for; each slider's source says how. One outside figure supports two settings in a row: the chance a wrong entry is accepted, and the chance it then spoils the work.
- **Two guards on impossible draws.** If a draw makes 'all parts' plus 'some parts' exceed certainty, both are scaled down in proportion; the three ceilings on what the library can hold likewise. With the current ranges neither happens.
- **The step match is drawn by hand.** The walkthroughs' ten steps and the model's stages are matched by a table, shown on the map. A limitation is placed on the map through that table and through its unknowns.
